title: Choose the visual world for the Merchant Portal
question: The roll assigned Arrivals Hall. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Arrivals Hall
options.lineage: Singapore airport arrivals boards and terminal signage
options.thesis: Every payment is a traveller heading to your bank; the portal is the arrivals board that says where your money is and when it lands.
options.viewport: Home opens on the plain-English headline as the board header, a monumental 'Next to land: $1,948.10 tomorrow', and the Money-arriving board: date, from (channel), amount, status in words (Landed / On time / Delayed, we are checking).
options.risk: A dark board can feel like transport, not a shop, and long boards can drift into the density you ruled out.

raised.raise: Each arrival row draws its transit time as a bar whose length is the real days from sale to bank.
One figure owns each screen; everything else stays quiet.
A head rule always names the span you are looking at, e.g. 'Showing 3 to 9 Nov'.
Items you have checked get circled and stay marked.
Status changes repaint a row in place; the board never reflows.

options.label: Stall Lightbox
options.lineage: hawker stall lightbox signboards and numbered menu panels
options.thesis: The portal talks like your stall's signboard: numbered panels, huge prices, nothing extra.
options.viewport: Home as a row of lit panels, No. 1 Money in today, No. 2 Coming to your bank, No. 3 Needs a look, each with a giant number and one button.
options.risk: The most obvious local reference, and it can tip into the kitsch or playful look you said to avoid.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: The portal shows only your next decision, one yellow band at a time.
options.viewport: Home as one band: 'Next: 3 payments need a look, about 2 minutes', with a monumental count and one arrow-button.
options.case: Fuses well: 'one main action per screen' becomes the next-decision band; wins on clarity but merchants manage money, not route through a terminal.
options.risk: Hides the overview accountants and Tan & Sons need; yellow everywhere tires fast.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Payments as rows on a flapping departure board.
options.viewport: A full-screen board of payment rows.
options.case: Same family as the roll, colder and less local; loses both axes.
options.kept: Status changes repaint a row in place; the board never reflows.
options.risk: Caps-heavy dark board, hard to read on a phone outdoors.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: Time drawn exactly as length on a vertical staff.
options.viewport: A rising staff of sales blocks.
options.case: Abstract notation no merchant reads; loses both axes.
options.kept: Transit time drawn as a bar whose length is the real days.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything a catalog number, labels as colour codes.
options.case: Codes instead of words breaks the plain-words rule; loses both axes.
options.kept: One figure owns each screen; everything else stays quiet.

options.label: Lexicon Page
options.thesis: Dense text columns with guide words at the head.
options.viewport: Columns of entries under guide words.
options.case: Dense and bookish, the opposite of hawker-simple; loses both axes.
options.kept: A head rule always names the span you are looking at.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Thousands of stamp-sized cells, circled in pen.
options.viewport: A packed grid of tiny cells.
options.case: Tiny dense cells fail both audiences; loses both axes.
options.kept: Items you have checked get circled and stay marked.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean merchant dashboard like the big payment providers ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, KPI cards, a sales chart and a recent-payments table.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other payment portal by design.
